chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal from Abu Ishaq from Muyassir from Jabr from al-Haytham ibn Abd al-Aziz from Sharih, who said:
Two litigants came to Ali (peace be upon him). One of them said, 'This man sold me a sheep that eats flies.' Sharih said, 'Good milk without feed.' He said, 'So he did not reject it.'

key_terms.تَأْكُلُ الذِّبَّانَ: Eats flies (indicating thinness or specific condition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling an animal with a defect in its feed or consumption according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *gharar* (ambiguity) and quality assessment in commercial transactions, where Imam Ali (AS) accepted the sale despite the sheep's thinness, validating the seller's claim of good milk. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the actual condition of the commodity at the time of sale rather than speculative defects, reflecting the practical legal acumen of the Imams in resolving market disputes. The hadith serves as a precedent for evaluating livestock sales based on observable utility rather than subjective complaints about physical appearance.
